kind: Already-scaled Native polygon reconstruction: isolated functional and operation proof
integrationStatus: Isolated helper only. No polygon worker protocol, Native-site fact consumption, pool dispatch or benchmark activation is introduced by this slice. No local elapsed-time comparison or speed claim.
originalBoundary: Original conductors, circle/pour/wire polygons, original intern calls and scaled-polygon memo hits/misses complete before the Flatbush polygon-bounds index finishes.
The isolated oracle captures the existing already-scaled Native polygon at that boundary. It never regenerates copper from original source objects or applies scaling a second time.

Every face and edge keeps original iteration order. Segment raw ps/pe coordinates and Arc raw pc/r/startAngle/endAngle/counterClockwise fields are copied without arithmetic. Fresh Native constructors reproduce the ordered face/edge/PlanarSet state used by the original contact predicate.

Original main polygons, Native constructor boundaries, original contact-query sequence, primitive memo hits/misses/FIFO eviction, graph connections and final error construction remain unchanged in the oracle.

Each actual original polygon-contact miss first executes the original predicate, then compares its boolean with reconstructed Native geometry. Entire cyclic owned polygon/face/edge/index data is checked before and after original queries and independent reconstructed queries; no getter is called by the state snapshot.

The helper does not grant admission. Future production preparation requires the complete existing private Native checker guard, genuine native executor brand/capacity admission, an upfront finite/resource-domain preflight, and only original fresh-miss tasks.

Future protocol validation must validate every row including unused rows. Reconstruction constructor faults are infrastructure/context faults, distinct from per-row Native query exceptions. Typed query exception facts must reproduce the original main predicate at its original ordered miss site; no error object is transferred into the final output.
All graph/error objects and their source aliases remain main-thread-owned. The worker-facing result is a pure boolean fact, not Native polygon or graph publication.
